findings.summary: Every page title names the chapter of only its first leftover block while the bulk of that page teaches the next chapter, so a learner navigating by title lands on the wrong section.
findings.evidence: Page 4 is `"page_title":"Object Types and Fields"` but after one N+1 callout it runs `"heading","text":"Closed Set Of Values"` and covers all of enums; page 5 is `"page_title":"Enums: Closed Sets of Values"` but its body is `"heading","text":"Only Two Wrappers"` … `"Null Propagation"`; the whole scalars chapter sits under `"page_title":"The Schema Is the Contract (cont.)"`. Only slide 2 carries `"cont":true`, although slides 3–8 are equally continuations.
findings.fix: Title each page for the chapter that occupies its body and mark the leftover tail with the `(cont.)` convention already used on slide 2 — e.g. retitle slide 3 "Object Types and Fields", slide 4 "Enums: Closed Sets of Values", slide 5 "Non-Null and Lists", and set `"cont":true` on slides 3–8.

findings.summary: The caption promises ten pages and names topics that have no corresponding titles in the eight-title set.
findings.evidence: Caption: "Ten pages on the type system ... scalars, objects, enums, wrappers, interfaces, unions, execution, and the change-safety table worth memorising." Titles supplied: 8 entries ending at "Unions: One Field, Unrelated Types" — none covering execution or the change-safety table.
findings.fix: Either add the missing execution and change-safety pages (with titles) to reach ten, or change the caption to "Eight pages" and drop "execution, and the change-safety table worth memorising" from the topic list so the promise matches the deck.

findings.summary: Page 1 ends with an orphan code block teaching the variable-strictness validation rule, which uses non-null and query variables hundreds of slides before either is introduced.
findings.evidence: `["query ($x: String) { f(arg: $x) }","# invalid if arg is String! and $x","# has no default value"]` appears immediately after the bullets "`__schema` and `__type` expose the schema at runtime" / "That powers GraphiQL, codegen and client type safety", with no heading or bullet referring to it. Arguments are introduced on page 3, `!` on page 5, and the rule itself belongs to the validation chapter ("Variable declaration must be at least as strict as the argument it fills").
findings.fix: Delete this block from page 1 and place it on the validation/execution page (slide 8) under the "Request Lifecycle" section, preceded by the bullet stating that a variable declaration must be at least as strict as the argument it fills.

findings.summary: The claim that only object types can carry a selection set is wrong — interfaces and unions are composite types and also require selection sets.
findings.evidence: "Only object types can carry a selection set" (bullet under "Object Type Anatomy"), which the same deck contradicts later with `node(id: $id) { __typename id ... on User { email } }` and `search(q: $q) { __typename ... on User { name } }`.
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Only composite types — object, interface, union — can carry a selection set" (leaf types, scalars and enums, cannot).

findings.summary: The input/output card asserts inputs are "cycle-safe by nullability" with no example or explanation, and the same page names list and non-null wrappers, which are not taught until page 5.
findings.evidence: Card `"title":"`input` (input)"` line "Cycle-safe by nullability"; and the callout "Argument types must be input types: scalars, enums, input objects and their list or non-null wrappers." Non-null and lists are first defined two pages later under `"heading","text":"Only Two Wrappers"`.
findings.fix: Replace "Cycle-safe by nullability" with a one-line SDL example showing a self-referencing input whose cycle terminates because the field is nullable (e.g. `input Filter { and: [Filter!] }` with a note that a client can stop by omitting it), or defer the point to the wrapping-types page once `!` has been defined.

findings.summary: The List Resilience table says a failed item in `[Post!]!` leaves the list nullified, but a non-null list cannot hold null, so the null propagates past the list to the nearest nullable ancestor.
findings.evidence: Table row: ["`[Post!]!`","whole list nullified"] — contradicting the page's own rule "The null lands at the nearest nullable parent".
findings.fix: Change the cell to something like "list can't be null — bubbles to the nearest nullable parent field".

findings.summary: In the "SEEN EVERYWHERE" callout the enum line overflows the box's right border and collides with the right-hand column's bullet text.
findings.evidence: "OrderStatus { PENDING SHIPPED CANCELLED }" — the "CANCELLED" text crosses the orange box border and the closing "}" sits outside the box on top of the bullet marker for "Wrappers compose and read inside-out"
findings.fix: Wrap or shrink the code line inside the callout (soft-wrap long monospace lines to the box width, or shorten the example to `OrderStatus { PENDING SHIPPED }`) so no glyph renders past the box border.

findings.summary: The caption advertises ten pages but the deck contains eight.
findings.evidence: caption: "Ten pages on the type system that decides all of it"; the `slides` array has 8 entries (Contract, Contract cont., Scalars, Object Types, Enums, Non-Null and Lists, Interfaces, Unions).

findings.summary: "Selection set" — the property that defines a leaf type — is used from page 2 on but is never defined or shown.
findings.evidence: Page 2: "They are leaf types — no selection set allowed"; page 3: "Only object types can carry a selection set"; page 4: "# leaf type — no selection set". The first query with a nested selection set does not appear until page 4 (`query { users(role: ADMIN) { id } }`).
findings.fix: On page 1, after the minimal-schema example, add one query example with its braces labelled (`{ me { id name } }  # the braces are a selection set`) so the term has a referent before scalars rely on it.

findings.summary: Deprecated enum values do not vanish from introspection — they are merely excluded by default and are returned when `includeDeprecated: true` is passed.
findings.evidence: "Deprecated values stay valid, vanish from introspection"; the spec defines `enumValues(includeDeprecated: Boolean = false)`, and graphql-js's standard `getIntrospectionQuery()` requests `enumValues(includeDeprecated: true)`, so GraphiQL and codegen still see them, flagged `isDeprecated`.
findings.fix: Reword to "Deprecated values stay valid; hidden from introspection unless `includeDeprecated: true`".

findings.summary: The row for `[Post]` implies a single failed item can nullify the list, which nullable item types prevent.
findings.evidence: Table row: ["`[Post]`","item `null`, rest survives"] is stated instead as "item `null`, list may go null".
findings.fix: Change to "item `null`, rest survives (list only nulls if the list field itself errors)".

findings.summary: Two list items in the "SEEN EVERYWHERE" callout render their leading dash alone on one line with the content orphaned onto the next.
findings.evidence: lines read "-" then "OrderStatus { PENDING SHIPPED CANCELLED }", and "-" then "CacheControlScope { PUBLIC PRIVATE }"
findings.fix: Keep the bullet dash and its code span on the same line (hanging-indent the wrapped code rather than breaking immediately after the marker).

findings.summary: The interface query example is built on the `node(id:)` root field, which is not introduced until the following page.
findings.evidence: Page 6 code `["node(id: $id) {","  __typename","  id                 # shared field","  ... on User { email }","}"]`; the field is only explained on page 7 under `"heading","text":"The `Node` Pattern"` ("`node(id: ID!): Node` refetches any object by global ID").
findings.fix: Either use a plainly-defined root field in the page 6 example (e.g. `search(q: $q)` returning `Node`) or move the two `Node`-pattern bullets forward so the refetch field is defined before the query that uses it.

findings.summary: The callout claims execution errors without `resolveType` or `isTypeOf`, ignoring the default type resolver's `__typename` strategy.
findings.evidence: "Supply `resolveType` on the interface, or `isTypeOf` on each type. Without one, execution errors at runtime." graphql-js's `defaultTypeResolver` first checks whether the resolved value carries a string `__typename` and only then falls back to `isTypeOf`.
findings.fix: Add the third option: "…or return a `__typename` on the value — the default type resolver reads it. With none of the three, execution errors at runtime."

findings.summary: The interface-implements-interface example appears as a bare code block with no bullet or heading stating that interfaces may implement other interfaces.
findings.evidence: Code `["interface Resource implements Node {","  id: ID!     # must re-declare it","  url: String!","}"]` sits under `"heading","text":"Implementer Freedom"` whose bullets only cover covariant returns and `type User implements Node & Actor`.
findings.fix: Add a bullet before the block — "Interfaces can implement interfaces (2020 spec) and must re-declare the inherited fields" — so the example has a claim to illustrate.
